title: Large pregnancy study shows Ozempic and Wegovy linked to premature birth risk when used for diabetes
summary: A Danish study of 756,636 pregnancies found that GLP-1 drugs (semaglutide, liraglutide) were not linked to increased pregnancy complications when prescribed for weight loss. However, when prescribed for diabetes, early exposure was associated with higher premature birth risk, likely driven by diabet
takeaways: Study of 756,636 pregnancies in Denmark (Oct 2009–Dec 2023)
No increased complications when GLP-1s used for weight loss
Higher premature birth risk (before 37 weeks) with diabetes prescriptions
Published in Human Reproduction Open
Current clinical guidance: stop GLP-1s 8 weeks before pregnancy planning
Guidance based on early-phase lab studies, not real-world evidence
Diabetes, not medication, likely drives premature birth risk

summary: An NIH study published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology found that women with higher blood levels of two "forever chemicals"—perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS)—had up to 93% higher rates of estrogen receptor-negative (ER-negative) breast cancer. title: Energy drinks linked to 11× higher cardiac arrest reports in new study
summary: A study presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026 found energy drinks and stimulant supplements associated with 11× more cardiac arrest reports and 4.5× more heart attack reports. Young adults ages 18–34 comprised nearly half of severe cases; some products contain 3–12×
takeaways: Energy drinks/stimulants vs. products without: 11× cardiac arrest reports, 4.5× heart attack reports
Young adults (18–34): nearly 50% of severe cardiovascular emergencies
Some energy drinks: 3× coffee's caffeine per fluid ounce; supplements 12× coffee's concentration
FDA classifies as foods/supplements, exempting from drug safety testing requirements
Energy drink industry sales 2024: $20+ billion (double from decade prior)

title: United States at risk of losing measles elimination status due to ongoing outbreaks
summary: The United States faces potential loss of its measles elimination status following recent outbreaks. A WHO regional committee is expected to decide this week whether the U.S. retains the status it achieved in 2000.
takeaways: At least 8 measles deaths reported in 2026
Decision expected from Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) committee this week
Loss of status previously described as unavoidable consequence of transmission patterns

title: Study reveals viral infections cause lasting immune system damage despite symptom resolution
summary: Research at Pompeu Fabra University found that mice recovering from acute viral infections experienced lasting immune system damage despite eliminating the virus. takeaways: Study published in Cell Death & Disease
Lasting immune damage observed despite viral clearance
Spleen changes included fibrosis and disrupted immune cell positioning
T cell activation impaired
Pre-infection vaccination prevented harmful immune system changes

title: Stopping statins after age 70 may be safer than expected, but long-term risks remain
summary: A study of nearly 1,900 adults aged 70+ found stopping statins appeared relatively safe short-term for people without prior heart attacks or strokes, but longer-term follow-up revealed higher rates of serious cardiovascular events or death. The findings contradict assumptions underlying current stat
takeaways: Study of ~1,900 adults aged 70+
Primary prevention without prior cardiovascular events
All participants had ≥2 chronic conditions
Follow-up: ~2 years, some extending to 4 years
Short-term discontinuation appears relatively safe
Longer follow-up: higher serious CV events/death rate
American Heart Association 2026 guideline recommends lifestyle, potentially medication for younger people

title: All of Us study identifies thousands of new genetic variants affecting drug response
summary: The All of Us study, conducted using data from the National Institutes of Health's All of Us program, analyzed nearly 100,000 Americans and identified thousands of new genetic variants in 16 pharmacogenes that influence responses to prescription drugs. title: Scientists map basal ganglia brain region implicated in psychiatric and neurologic disorders
summary: A major research collaboration produced the most detailed map of the basal ganglia, identifying over 25 million cells and their types. The work revealed a new neuron type implicated in schizophrenia and cell types linked to depression, bipolar disorder, and PTSD; targeted gene therapy proved as effe
takeaways: Profiled more than 25 million cells
Discovered new neuron type implicated in schizophrenia
Identified cell types linked to depression, bipolar disorder, PTSD
Targeted gene therapy as effective as blanket approach in Parkinson's models

title: Occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher stroke risk
summary: A study of 440,000+ Americans presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026 found occasional marijuana use associated with 40% higher odds of reporting stroke history. The association held across consumption methods and was not limited to frequent users.
takeaways: Occasional cannabis use: 40% higher stroke history odds
Study population: 440,000+ Americans (BRFSS data 2020–2024)
U.S. cannabis use surge: 1 in 6 adults in 2024 vs. 1 in 10 in 2020 (51% increase)
Association established, causation not proven; affects all consumption methods

title: Bioengineered chewing gum reduces HPV levels by up to 93% in cancer patients
summary: University of Pennsylvania scientists developed a bioengineered chewing gum containing plant-based proteins that reduced HPV levels by up to 93% in laboratory tests using oral samples from head and neck cancer patients. takeaways: HPV reduction: up to 93% in lab tests on patient oral samples
Bacterial impact: nearly eliminated Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum; preserved beneficial oral bacteria
HPV, Pg, Fn linked to oropharyngeal cancer development and worsened survival
Published in Scientific Reports
Potential for affordable treatment supporting cancer prevention and existing therapies

title: TRF2 protein discovered crucial for muscle stem cell regeneration and preventing fibrosis
summary: Researchers found that TRF2, known for chromosome protection, plays a critical role in muscle stem cell identity and regeneration, with implications for muscular dystrophy treatment.

title: Brain Differences in Strategy Switching May Explain Childhood Math Struggles
summary: Stanford researchers found that children with persistent math difficulty show slower strategy-switching and reduced responsiveness to problem difficulty changes.

title: Scientists find fructose may enable aggressive ovarian cancer cells to spread
summary: Researchers discovered that fructose, commonly found in sweetened foods, may help chemotherapy-resistant ovarian cancer cells weaken tumor cell bonds and metastasize.

title: Biogen Expects Pivotal Lupus Trial Readout
summary: Biogen is preparing to release results from pivotal clinical trials of an experimental lupus therapy.

title: Blackstone backs Pfizer's $10 billion Metsera obesity drug acquisition
summary: Pfizer brought in private equity firm Blackstone to help finance its $10 billion acquisition of Metsera for monthly obesity treatment development.

title: Obesity paradox: overweight dementia patients show 16–27% lower mortality
summary: A study of 4,500+ older adults found that overweight and obese individuals diagnosed with dementia had 16–27% lower death risk than normal-weight peers, possibly due to greater metabolic reserves.

title: Preventive Care Panel Members Hold Significant Pharma and Medical Practice Financial Interests
summary: Federal filings reveal that US Preventive Services Task Force panelists hold substantial conflicts of interest including pharma stocks and private practices, despite ethics waivers.

title: Drug companies explore workarounds to protect U.S. sales amid president's most-favored-nations drug pricing policy
summary: Pharmaceutical manufacturers are developing strategies to shield domestic revenues in response to the president's most-favored-nations policy affecting drug pricing.

title: Alternative BMI metrics could flip obesity diagnosis for millions
summary: A newly proposed obesity identification method could reclassify millions of people, potentially enabling more targeted medical care.

title: Study links animal protein to lower testosterone, plant protein to higher levels
summary: Research on 2,500+ men found higher animal protein intake, particularly from dairy, associated with lower testosterone, while plant protein correlated with higher levels.

title: STAT investigation reveals risks in unproven three-parent IVF industry
summary: A STAT investigation found that fertility clinics are offering an unproven three-parent IVF procedure to older women as part of a growing fertility tourism industry.

title: Peptide Therapies: Promise and Health Risks Under Scrutiny
summary: Peptide-based treatments are gaining popularity but their safety and efficacy remain contested.

title: Study: high-intensity sports with explosive movements more effective than walking or weight training for bone strength
summary: A study suggests that walking and weight training alone may not adequately maintain bone strength.

title: MDCalc Launches CrossCover Tool to Help Doctors Verify AI Medical Chatbot Answers
summary: MDCalc introduces CrossCover, a verification tool designed to increase clinician confidence in generative AI medical reference systems.

title: Healthcare Providers Sue Employers Over Out-of-Network Medical Bill Disputes
summary: Medical providers increasingly pursue legal action against employers, claiming responsibility for out-of-network bills insurers have delayed or underpaid.

title: Oura's acquisition of health startup raises Eli Lilly conflict-of-interest concerns
summary: Oura's acquisition of a telehealth startup that markets GLP-1s raises conflict-of-interest questions regarding its relationship with pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly.

title: Alnylam's Amvuttra Heart Drug Faces Sales Slowdown, Threatening Biotech Growth
summary: Alnylam, once positioned to reach $100 billion valuation, is struggling as sales of its heart drug Amvuttra decelerate.

title: Newly elected doctors and scientists aim to restore public trust in science
summary: Scores of doctors and scientists were elected to office last week, raising hopes they can help rebuild public confidence in scientific institutions.

title: Youth-led experiments across the U.S. address phone addiction and reclaim attention
summary: Young people across the United States are conducting homegrown experiments to reduce phone addiction and push back against technology industry practices.
